- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly to capture momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, model exhibits mean-reversion bias; align forecast with recent 7–14 day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen forecast by 0.5–1.5% if sentiment changes abruptly within 5 days prior.
- If sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, model may overcorrect; reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid “sentiment-driven overbought” traps.
